 Follow A Woman Got Dumped, Opened Wine, And Gained The "Chicago Fire" Cast As Her Hype Squad
 Anna Good Wed, November 11, 2026 at 9:32 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A local Chicago woman has gone viral after being dumped and ending up with the cast of NBC's Chicago Fire as her own personal hype squad, mocking her ex and telling him about how badly he screwed up.
 NBC / Getty Images
 As a reminder, Season 15 of Chicago Fire only just started airing at the beginning of October. While there have been a number of dramatic changes on the show recently, there are no spoilers here! Mum's the word.
 NBC / Getty Images
 Now, back to the heartbreak. TikToker Grace Hackett ( @gracehacket ) uploaded a video to TikTok on Nov. 10, 2026, with a text overlay that reads, "POV. Walking back home after you got dumped. Time to go watch Chicago Fire ."
 @gracehacket / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Related: "These 37 Fails From Last Week Made Me Laugh So Hard I Think I Have Abs Now" 
 The viral TikTok video shows Hackett standing on the street late at night next to actor Christian Stolte, who plays Randall "Mouch" McHolland on the firefighting show, with a bottle of wine in hand.
 NBC / Getty Images
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the quick video, Stolte leans toward the camera, asking, "Hey, boy, did you screw up, Joe. You've made a huge mistake."
 @gracehacket / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Co-star Taylor Kinney then chimes in, "What were you thinking, Joe?"
 NBC / Getty Images
 Several of his Chicago Fire castmates are seated on the steps nearby and also joined in on the roasting.
 @gracehacket / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Related: "Are These People Actually The A-Hole Or Not?" 
 Stolte went on to add, "Wait, wait, wait, we're going to spend the rest of the night fighting over who gets to take this lady home and drink some wine with her, ok? You f**ked up, Joe, sorry."
 @gracehacket / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Advertisement Advertisement The actors were so clearly doing what they could to make Hackett laugh, and they seemed to have succeeded at their mission, cheering as they called her ex a "jerk."
 @gracehacket / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 While we don't yet know any of the surrounding details about the relationship's end, the brokenhearted woman wrote in the caption, "Love a supportive cast! And walking through a TV set post breakup."
 Peter Gordon / NBC / Getty Images
 Related: "40 Shocking Photos Of People Cheating Death" 
 Her video has over 1.8 million views and counting, and folks in the comments and elsewhere online are loving the supportive vibes from the cast.
 @rara_1234567891011 / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 One commenter wrote, "The biggest flex to have the CHICAGO FIRE squad on your side in the breakup ❣️"
 @dana_ess / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Advertisement Advertisement Another person added, "If Mouch told me I f***ed up, I'd have to re evaluate my life choices 😭"
 @v1v1enne420 / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 It's honestly a pretty iconic way to deal with a breakup.
 @kayleighosullvn_ / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 And this woman even shared how accurate this kind of behavior is to real-life firefighters!
 @peepo_girl / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Related: "Ex-Cult Members Are Sharing The Moments They Realized Something Was Wrong" 
 Many said that this level of hype would heal them...
 @user877665512 / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Advertisement Advertisement ...especially coming from the cast of their favorite TV show.
 @jordannarants / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 It might even be "the most iconic way to go through a breakup."
 @caroline_svarre98 / TikTok / Via tiktok.com 
 Hackett later wrote in the comments section of her video, "These comments are healing me," so it seems like the combined efforts of the Chicago Fire squad and the internet seemed to do the trick!
